Submission readiness: NOT READY

Computed from this object's own state — a structural condition is unmet. This is not a fixed disclaimer: the conditions below are each testable, and a build in which they are met renders READY.

  • No registration evidence — This object records no protocol registration.
  • Publication bias not assessable (no attestation can discharge this) — The GRADE publication-bias domain for this outcome is rated not assessable. No attestation changes that; it is a property of how many studies there are.

Qualifications that travel with the headline

  • The pooled benefit depends on no single trial. Every leave-one-out fit keeps the null outside its interval and every one lands close to the full pool. This is the opposite of what the companion reduced-ejection-fraction review in this batch found, where dropping the largest trial removed the benefit, and the contrast is worth stating because the two objects share a template and a reader may assume they share a fragility. They do not.

SGLT2 inhibitors against placebo in chronic heart failure across the ejection fraction spectrum: the four randomised outcome trials that report cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event as a time-to-first hazard ratio

In adults with chronic heart failure, what is the hazard of a first cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure event with an SGLT2 inhibitor compared with placebo added to background therapy?

In this section: Registration and administrative information (PROSPERO field set) · What this object claims to contain

Eligibility criteriaEligibility turns on population, intervention and comparator: a trial is in scope if it randomised adults with chronic heart failure to an SGLT2 inhibitor against placebo on top of background therapy. It does not turn on which analysis the trial reported, because section 3.2.4 cautions that making eligibility depend on reported outcomes invites outcome reporting bias. What the measure governs is pooling, under section 10.9: only a time-to-first-event hazard ratio can be combined with the others. Each row below therefore carries two separate columns -- the eligibility axis it fails, and, where it applies, the reason its quantity could not have been pooled even had it been eligible. What this object claims to contain

Full build, with a stated boundary on the search. Every randomised trial reached by reconciliation against three published syntheses of this class in heart failure, and by the registry records staged for every trial those syntheses name, is either pooled or in one screening log with the criterion it fails and the quantity it reports instead. There is exactly one source list, `screening.records`. The object also holds `screening.excluded`, which is not a second table a reader must reconcile: it is a view computed from the records at build time, row for row, so it cannot say anything the records do not. What this statement does not claim is a systematic database search; none was run, the limitation is recorded in the screening block, and a trial missed by all three syntheses and absent from the staged registry layer would be missed here.

In this section: SOLOIST-WHF NCT03521934 · PMID 33200892 · Scored NCT03315143 · PMID 33200891 · Empulse NCT04157751 · PMID 35228754

SOLOIST-WHF NCT03521934 · PMID 33200892

This review's decision: excluded.

Population, which is the axis the Handbook makes an eligibility criterion. It enrolled patients with type 2 diabetes who had been hospitalized for worsening heart failure and started treatment before or shortly after discharge, which is a recently-decompensated population rather than the chronic ambulatory one this question fixes. Separately, and recorded as a pooling limit rather than as a second exclusion: its primary endpoint is the total number of cardiovascular deaths, heart failure hospitalizations and urgent heart failure visits -- first and subsequent events -- which its own abstract states in those words. That is a recurrent-event quantity, so under section 10.9 it could not have entered this pool even had the population matched. The two are kept apart because an earlier version of this object ran them together and cited a section that cautions against exactly that.

  • population

What it actually reports: a hazard ratio for the total occurrence of the composite, reported as 0.67 with a 95% interval of 0.52 to 0.85 by its publication and its registry record alike

Why that is not this review's measure: It IS labelled a hazard ratio by every layer that reports it, and that is exactly the trap. A recurrent-event analysis counts a participant each time they have an event; a time-to-first analysis counts them once. The two share a name, a scale and a direction, so storing this value in the same field as the four pooled cells would be invisible to a reader and to most software. The detector that guards effect-measure form would not catch it either, because both are hazard ratios. It is stored nowhere in this object except in this sentence.

primary_oa: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33200892/

Scored NCT03315143 · PMID 33200891

This review's decision: excluded.

Population, and this is the one exclusion in this log that does not turn on the measure. It enrolled patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease at cardiovascular risk; heart failure was not an entry requirement and most participants did not have it. It is a cardiovascular and renal outcome trial in diabetic kidney disease, not a heart failure trial, so it fails the first axis of the question.

  • population

What it actually reports: its changed primary endpoint is a TOTAL-occurrence composite; but it also reports its original co-primary, the first occurrence of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, as a hazard ratio of 0.77 with a 95% interval of 0.66 to 0.91

Why that is not this review's measure: It is not stored because of the population, not because of its form. This row says so explicitly because the honest version of this exclusion is uncomfortable: a first-event hazard ratio for this review's exact composite exists for this trial and is quoted above, so a reader cannot be told the quantity was unavailable. The trial is out on who was enrolled. A reader who disagrees with that boundary can see precisely what including it would have added, which is the point of recording the value here.

primary_oa: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33200891/

Empulse NCT04157751 · PMID 35228754

This review's decision: excluded.

Population and duration: patients were randomised in hospital during an admission for acute heart failure and treated for up to ninety days, which is neither the chronic population nor the event-driven follow-up this question fixes. Separately, as a pooling limit and not as a second exclusion: its primary outcome is clinical benefit expressed as a hierarchical composite of death, heart failure events and a symptom-score difference, analysed as a stratified win ratio -- a ratio of favourable to unfavourable pairwise comparisons, with no interpretation as a hazard and with the opposite direction of benefit.

  • population

What it actually reports: a stratified win ratio of 1.36 with a 95% interval of 1.09 to 1.68, in which values above one favour treatment -- the opposite direction to every value this object pools

Why that is not this review's measure: Its direction of benefit is inverted relative to a hazard ratio, so storing it in a hazard-ratio field would not merely mislabel the quantity, it would reverse the sign of the trial's finding. Its registry record does also post a secondary first-occurrence hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or a heart failure event, and that value is not pooled either, on the population and duration grounds above.

What was measured

Table 7. What was measured
Comparatorplacebo added to background heart failure therapy
Estimandtime_to_first — Cox proportional hazards
Unit of analysisparticipant, with the time to the first component event
Case definitioneach trial's own primary composite of centrally adjudicated cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event, whichever occurs first. The trials do not define the worsening-heart-failure component identically -- two count an urgent heart failure visit and two count only hospitalization -- and the two that count it do not define it identically either, which is why each cell stores its own trial's wording rather than a common paraphrase. The FDA label records a further difference, in whether deaths of undetermined cause were counted as cardiovascular. All of it is in the uniformity table and none of it is harmonized away.
Windowfrom randomisation to the end of the trial's own follow-up
Analysis populationeach trial's own full analysis set, which on all four equals its randomised total
Effect scalereported on the log scale; nothing is pooled on this outcome

Pooled result

Estimate withdrawn. The four trials do not share one endpoint. DAPA-HF and DELIVER count cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, OR an urgent heart-failure visit; emperor-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved count cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure only. Two trials count an event class the other two do not, so this pool combined quantities that are not the same quantity. Verified word for word against each trial's registry entry rather than assumed.

The withdrawal was published on the page on 2026-08-17 and not in this object. The page carried a paragraph explaining the withdrawal while its Pooled result card still read HR 0.7785 (0.7296 to 0.8306) as the headline, and the estimator-comparison table printed the same value four more times: six occurrences of the withdrawn number against one occurrence of the word 'withdrawn'. The object kept it as a live point, so any rebuild would have re-published it in full. This is the withdraw-on-both-surfaces lesson -- logged in this repository after ABLATION_AF -- left open on the very topic that produced it.

Previously displayed: HR 0.7785 (0.7296 to 0.8306) — superseded by this withdrawal.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: Pool four trials reporting the same effect measure for the same outcome concept against the same comparator, producing an average across a documented difference in how two of them define the composite, across two molecules and across the ejection-fraction spectrum

Cochrane Handbook sections: 3.2.1, 3.2.3, 3.2.4, 10.9, 10.10.1, 10.10.2, 10.10.4, 10.14

Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.3 fix the two axes on which eligibility turns -- population and comparator -- and every screening decision names which of them it falls on, which is why the log has a criterion column rather than a verdict column. Section 3.2.4 is what keeps the measure out of that list: it cautions that eligibility resting on which outcomes a study reported invites outcome reporting bias, so the measure is recorded in a separate column as a limit on pooling. Section 10.9 is the authority for that limit, and it gives the hazard ratio as the effect measure for time-to-event data and sanctions combining log hazard ratios by generic inverse variance; all four trials report a Cox hazard ratio for the time to a first event of their primary composite against placebo, so the measure is shared and nothing is converted. What the pool crosses is documented under 10.10.1 in the uniformity table, and the first row of that table is the one that matters: two trials count an urgent heart failure visit inside the composite and two do not. That difference is not smoothed away, not harmonized and not described as absent. Section 10.10.4 governs the model and the between-study variance estimator; restricted maximum likelihood is used and the comparison of estimators that 10.10.4.4 motivates is RUN rather than asserted, and with this little heterogeneity the estimators agree closely, which is reported as the unremarkable result it is. Section 10.14 is why the leave-one-out analysis is here; unlike the other cardiology pool in this batch it changes nothing, and that is itself the finding.

Leave-one-out sensitivity

Two decisions. First, whether the pooled benefit depends on any single trial. Second, whether it depends on the choice of between-study variance estimator and interval method, which with four studies is not automatically a formality even though it turns out to be one here.

Table 11. Leave-one-out sensitivity
Cohort omittedkHR (95% CI)
dapa-hf30.7906 (0.7342 to 0.8513)
emperor-reduced30.7864 (0.731 to 0.8461)
emperor-preserved30.7749 (0.7194 to 0.8346)
deliver30.7602 (0.7029 to 0.822)

The pooled benefit depends on no single trial. Every leave-one-out fit keeps the null outside its interval and every one lands close to the full pool. This is the opposite of what the companion reduced-ejection-fraction review in this batch found, where dropping the largest trial removed the benefit, and the contrast is worth stating because the two objects share a template and a reader may assume they share a fragility. They do not.

Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.14: sensitivity analyses examine whether overall findings are robust to potentially influential decisions. Section 10.10.4.4 governs the estimator half -- it records that methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better and that restricted maximum likelihood is the RevMan default. Section 10.10.4.5 is about interpretation with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval, not the variance estimator; it is cited for the interval comparison and not for the estimator comparison.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

These are the WITHDRAWN pool's values. The estimate below is retired: the trials do not share one endpoint. The comparison is kept because it answers a real question -- whether the arithmetic depended on the estimator, and it did not -- and it does not rescue the pool, because the objection is to the ESTIMAND and no choice of between-study variance touches that.

Section 10.10.4.4 records that estimators other than DerSimonian and Laird perform better and that restricted maximum likelihood is now the default in the Cochrane software, and it is the whole of the authority for running this comparison. Nothing in the Handbook instructs a review to compare variance estimators at a particular number of studies; running it is a choice made under section 10.14. Here it is uninformative, and that is reported rather than dropped: a sensitivity analysis that changes nothing is evidence about the result, and only a lane that ran it can say so.

Table 12. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
Between-study varianceIntervalSummary (95% CI)τ²
DerSimonian-Laird (DL)ordinary (Wald)0.7785 (0.7296 to 0.8306)0
Paule-Mandel (PM)ordinary (Wald)0.7785 (0.7296 to 0.8306)0
restricted maximum likelihood (REML)ordinary (Wald)0.7785 (0.7296 to 0.8306)0
restricted maximum likelihood (REML)Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ)0.7785 (0.7007 to 0.8649)0

The three variance estimators agree, because there is no between-study variance for them to disagree about, and all three intervals exclude the null. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval is wider, as its floor guarantees it can only be, and it excludes the null as well. No method tried here reverses the finding. This is reported as a null sensitivity result and not as corroboration: four ways of computing an interval from the same four numbers agreeing is arithmetic, not independent evidence.

Restricted maximum likelihood is kept as the headline estimator with the ordinary interval, because section 10.10.4.4 records it as the Cochrane default and as a better estimator than DerSimonian and Laird. With the between-study variance estimated at zero the choice is close to immaterial here, and keeping the default is therefore not a choice that flatters the result. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval is reported beside it, with the floor on its scale factor applied so it can widen and can never come out narrower than the ordinary interval.

What was measured

Table 13. What was measured
Comparatorplacebo
Estimandtime_to_first — Cox proportional hazards, as reported by each trial
Unit of analysisparticipant, time to the first component event
Case definitioncardiovascular death OR hospitalisation for heart failure. Two components. An urgent heart-failure visit is not a qualifying event.
Effect scalereported on the natural scale; nothing is pooled on this outcome

Pooled result

HR 0.7636 (0.7062 to 0.8258), 95% interval

cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, first event. random-effects, estimator REML, k = 3.

τ² 0 · I² 0% · Q 0.3837 on 2 df

Read this beside the estimate. This outcome is the harmonised two-component composite -- cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure. That is the registered primary of EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved. It is not dapa-hf's: NCT03036124 registers a THREE-component primary that also counts an urgent heart-failure visit. The harmonisation is disclosed in this outcome's own name; what follows from it for risk of bias is recorded per result.

EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved register masking as double -- participant and investigator only. Their endpoints are adjudicated, which is the standard mitigation, but no registration states that the adjudicators were blinded. DAPA-HF is quadruple-masked.

Contributing trials

Table 14. Contributing trials
TrialAnalysed
treatment / control		 HR (95% CI), or events Source of this cell

Registered endpoint definitions read from every contributing registration on 2026-08-18; recorded per trial on this object.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 15. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML0.7636 (0.7062 to 0.8258)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 2 degree(s) of freedom (t = 4.3027)0.7636 (0.6431 to 0.9068)

The published point is 0.7636 and the house-rule point is 0.7636. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

The rating it carried was High, held in results.by_outcome.<oid>.grade; it is recorded here rather than shown in the certainty column.

It records nothing about what that quantity was measured against -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

The two share a name, a scale and a direction, so storing this value in the same field as the four pooled cells would be invisible to a reader and to most software. The detector that guards effect-measure form would not catch it either, because both are hazard ratios. It is stored nowhere in this object except in this sentence.

Established by test, not argument: widening this list from 9 fields to 14 halved gepotidacin's disagreement -- its entire selection of the reported result divergence was a fact the second assessor had never been shown -- and left ceftaroline and tigecycline unmoved.

What this review does not publishWhat this review does not publish. This review also examined one outcome for which no pooled estimate is published: Cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio (k=4) -- The four trials do not share one endpoint. Each of those outcomes is recorded on this review with the reason it was not pooled, and none of them contributes to the estimate reported above (0.7636 at k=3, 0.7835 at k=2). A reader meeting the pooled result should not take it as covering every outcome, or every trial, this review examined. This sentence exists because a second, independent reading -- by a different model family, given the object and the abstract and none of our conclusions -- found that a reader would reasonably conclude the review pools all relevant trials, and that the object does not support that. The withdrawals were already recorded beside the outcomes they concern; they were invisible from the abstract, which is where the impression forms.

The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.

Table 21. Certainty of the evidence (GRADE)
DomainRatingWhy it was rated that way
Risk of biasnot seriousEvery contributing trial is double-blind, randomised one to one against a matching placebo, prospectively registered, and posts results to its registry; the components of the composite are adjudicated by a central committee in each. This object holds each trial's registry record, its primary publication and two regulator documents, and the effect estimate agrees across all four layers on all four trials, which is a check on reporting rather than on conduct but is the check available. The endpoint pooled here is each trial's own primary, so none of the selective-reporting exposure that a secondary endpoint carries applies. No trial in this pool stopped early for benefit. Not downgraded.
Inconsistencynot serious—
Indirectnessnot seriousPopulation, intervention and comparator are all direct: adults with chronic heart failure, an SGLT2 inhibitor at its approved heart failure dose, against placebo on top of background therapy, with the outcome measured in the trials themselves and not surrogated. The one candidate for indirectness is the outcome, because two trials count an urgent heart failure visit within the composite and two do not. It is not downgraded, and the reasoning is stated rather than assumed: the extra component is a worsening-heart-failure event of the same clinical kind as the other two, it is the minority of events in both trials that count it, and the regulator layers report those trials' composites decomposed so the size of that minority is visible rather than inferred. A reader who wants the strictly harmonized composite instead has it in the reconciliation block, from syntheses that computed it, and this object does not pretend the two are the same quantity.
Imprecisionnot serious—
Publication biasnot assessable—

Paper

Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title

SGLT2 inhibitors against placebo in chronic heart failure across the ejection fraction spectrum: the four randomised outcome trials that report cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event as a time-to-first hazard ratio1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. title

Abstract

Question. In adults with chronic heart failure, what is the hazard of a first cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure event with an SGLT2 inhibitor compared with placebo added to background therapy?1

Methods. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 and PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) were searched; estimates were pooled under a random-effects model with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE.2

Results. Cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, first event: hazard ratio 0.764 (0.706 to 0.826) across 3 trials; Cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, or an urgent heart-failure visit, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio: 0.783 (0.709 to 0.866) across 2 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed closely (I-squared 0%); and certainty of the evidence was low.3

Introduction

Background. This review asks: In adults with chronic heart failure, what is the hazard of a first cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure event with an SGLT2 inhibitor compared with placebo added to background therapy? It pools 4 randomised trials, against placebo added to background heart failure therapy. The outcomes pooled are Cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio; cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, first event; Cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, or an urgent heart-failure visit, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio.1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. manuscript.introduction

Methods — search

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 -- query 1, narrower, and it missed an included trial on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: condition="chronic heart failure"; intervention="dapagliflozin OR empagliflozin OR sotagliflozin OR canagliflozin OR ertugliflozin"; study_type=interventional; phase=[PHASE3,PHASE4]; page_size=60. It returned 23 record(s). This query did not surface NCT03619213 (DELIVER), which is one of this object's own included trials. DELIVER registers its condition as 'Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction' -- no 'chronic' -- while DAPA-HF registers 'Chronic Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction'. A condition term one word narrower than the registry's own wording dropped an included trial. Recorded rather than replaced: a search that missed something is evidence about the search.1

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 -- query 2, broader, covers the included set on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: condition="heart failure"; intervention="dapagliflozin OR empagliflozin OR sotagliflozin OR canagliflozin OR ertugliflozin"; study_type=interventional; phase=[PHASE3]; page_size=100. It returned 56 record(s).2

Searches were executed in PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: (dapagliflozin[tiab] OR empagliflozin[tiab] OR sotagliflozin[tiab] OR "SGLT2 inhibitor"[tiab] OR "sodium-glucose cotransporter 2"[tiab]) and ("heart failure"[tiab] OR HFrEF[tiab] OR HFpEF[tiab]) and (randomized controlled trial[pt] OR randomised[tiab] OR randomized[tiab]). It returned 50 record(s).3

Methods — eligibility criteria

Eligibility turns on population, intervention and comparator: a trial is in scope if it randomised adults with chronic heart failure to an SGLT2 inhibitor against placebo on top of background therapy. It does not turn on which analysis the trial reported, because section 3.2.4 cautions that making eligibility depend on reported outcomes invites outcome reporting bias. What the measure governs is pooling, under section 10.9: only a time-to-first-event hazard ratio can be combined with the others. Each row below therefore carries two separate columns -- the eligibility axis it fails, and, where it applies, the reason its quantity could not have been pooled even had it been eligible. Every screened trial appears with the quantity it reports quoted, whichever column it fell in.1

Each criterion above is recorded with the source it was derived from in `screening.eligibility_provenance`; none is asserted here without one.2

Methods — outcomes sought at every registered rank

Before deciding which outcomes could be combined, every trial was read at every registered rank -- primary, secondary and other -- asking: does each trial report, at any rank -- primary, secondary or other -- an outcome matching what the others report, before any decision about which pools are possible? Reading only primaries would have shown DAPA-HF reporting a THREE-component endpoint and EMPEROR reporting a TWO-component one, and concluded they share nothing. DAPA-HF's two-component composite is at secondary rank. Asked at the primary alone, pool A does not exist.1

Methods — synthesis

For cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, first event, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

For cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, or an urgent heart-failure visit, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.2

Intervals are 95% confidence intervals.3

Methodological decisions follow Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al (editors). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. Cochrane, 2025., version 6.5.1, and the sections relied on are listed in the object rather than cited generically.4

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (22 August 2019 version, as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook), following Higgins JPT, Savovic J, Page MJ, Elbers RG, Sterne JAC. Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial. In: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. A result, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: 'risk of bias is assessed for a specific result'. Every judgement below names its outcome. 9 result-level assessments were made. A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is no information, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.5

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.6

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1, Chapter 14: Completing 'Summary of findings' tables and grading the certainty of the evidence. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down with reasons. 2 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP. Rating up for large effect or dose-response applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.7

Results

The pooled hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, first event was 0.764 (0.706 to 0.826, 95% interval) across 3 trials, against placebo.1

Noted on this pool. Read this beside the estimate. This outcome is the harmonised two-component composite -- cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure. That is the registered primary of EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved. It is not dapa-hf's: NCT03036124 registers a THREE-component primary that also counts an urgent heart-failure visit. The harmonisation is disclosed in this outcome's own name; what follows from it for risk of bias is recorded per result. EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved register masking as double -- participant and investigator only. Their endpoints are adjudicated, which is the standard mitigation, but no registration states that the adjudicators were blinded. DAPA-HF is quadruple-masked.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.384, on degrees of freedom 2.3

DELIVER (NCT03619213) does not post the first-event two-component outcome. Its registry secondaries are RECURRENT-EVENT composites (HR 0.77), which is a different quantity again. Its harmonised value exists in the publication, not the registration. A k=3 pool we can fully vouch for beats A k=4 with one input we cannot -- the same call made for INCRETIN_HFpEF.4

The original withdrawal was disproportionate and this page says so. The four trials genuinely do not share a primary endpoint -- DAPA-HF and DELIVER count an urgent heart-failure visit that the EMPEROR trials do not -- and that observation was correct. The remedy was not. A harmonised two-component endpoint was available: it is the EMPEROR trials' own primary, and DAPA-HF posts it as a secondary in the same registration we had already read. We withheld an estimate a reader needed and the data to give it was one rank down.5

What this does not establish: Not that the original four-trial pool was acceptable -- it combined quantities that were not the same quantity, and that withdrawal stands on this page with its reason. Not that these three trials are free of bias; no risk-of-bias assessment is recorded. Not a result for DELIVER's population, which is absent here.6

The pooled hazard ratio for cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, or an urgent heart-failure visit, whichever comes first was 0.783 (0.709 to 0.866, 95% interval) across 2 trials, against placebo.7

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 22.5%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0.0012, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 1.29, on degrees of freedom 1.8

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: Both trials register this same three-component composite as their primary endpoint. One endpoint definition, one question. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.9

This does not supersede the two-component pool and is not superseded by it. They estimate the effect on different composite endpoints. The k=4 pool that mixed the two definitions remains withdrawn.10

Cardiovascular death or a worsening heart failure event, whichever comes first, as a hazard ratio. These 4 trials are not pooled, and the reason is stated rather than the outcome being quietly omitted: The four trials do not share one endpoint. DAPA-HF and DELIVER count cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, or an urgent heart-failure visit; emperor-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved count cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure only. Two trials count an event class the other two do not, so this pool combined quantities that are not the same quantity. Verified word for word against each trial's registry entry rather than assumed.11

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.12

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down with reasons.1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for large effect or dose-response applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

risk_of_bias -1 inconsistency +0 indirectness +0 imprecision -1 publication bias +03

risk_of_bias -1 inconsistency +0 indirectness +0 imprecision -1 publication bias +04

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: selection of the reported result on 5 result(s), the randomisation process on 4 result(s), measurement of the outcome on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.5

Limitations

Known limitation of the screen: No fresh systematic database search was run for this object, and nothing here should be read as though one had been. The completeness claim rests on reconciliation against three independent published syntheses whose included-study lists are read rather than counted, plus the registry layer. A trial that all three syntheses missed and that no staged registry record names would be missed here too. That is a real and stated limit on the search, and it is the reason the completeness statement below is scoped to what was reconciled against rather than to the literature as a whole.1

Eligible trials that do not contribute: No trial is in this category. Every trial meeting the population, the comparator and the measure contributes; every trial failing one of the three is in the screening log with the criterion it fails. This field is present and empty rather than absent, so a reader can tell the category was considered.2

This review does not claim no internal check is described as independent verification. A script that reads this object and reports that this object is consistent has confirmed consistency and nothing else, and a badge that cannot fail is worth less than no badge, because it teaches a reader to stop looking. The validator finding no defect is reported as exactly that.3

4 claim(s) previously made about this review were corrected and the corrections are retained on the object rather than overwritten.4

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.5

restated_2026_08_19_placebo_discriminatork3 was 36, k3 now 46, delta 10, why topic_identity.locate() read the registry's arm TYPES literally. Some registrations declare NO arm typed EXPERIMENTAL: AFFIRM-AHF and HEART-FID both type their active drug ACTIVE_COMPARATOR against a PLACEBO_COMPARATOR arm. The classifier called the intervention a comparator and silently shrank the evidence base. Rule adopted: PLACEBO IS NEVER THE INTERVENTION, so a drug compared against it is -- but where the other arm is an ACTIVE drug, the topic drug genuinely is one of two comparators and the rule must not fire., why this is a correction not a relaxation It moved counts in BOTH directions across the corpus: sglt2-hf +10, bempedoic-acid-review -1. The executed search surfaced this object's OWN included trials, and the arm-role classifier then refused to recognise two of them as the intervention. Neither instrument found it alone. This is the first defect tonight found in the WITHHOLDING direction by an instrument rather than by a person noticing -- the class we had said has no guard., trials no longer experimental —, screening status after restatement 46 experimental, 4 included, 32 already screened, 10 NEWLY UNSCREENED. The withholding question, asked at every rank

does each trial report, AT ANY RANK -- primary, secondary or other -- an outcome matching what the others report, before any decision about which pools are possible?

Reading only primaries would have shown DAPA-HF reporting a THREE-component endpoint and EMPEROR reporting a TWO-component one, and concluded they share nothing. DAPA-HF's two-component composite is at SECONDARY rank. Asked at the primary alone, pool A does not exist.

NCT03619213DELIVERNONE AT ANY RANK. Every heart-failure composite it registers -- primary and secondary -- includes an urgent heart-failure visit. This is why pool A is k=3 and not k=4, and it is established by reading all seven ranks rather than by matching the primary.PRIMARY

A matcher defect, found and not relied on

The first pass used a substring matcher for the two-component endpoint. It returned ZERO for BOTH EMPEROR trials, whose primaries ARE the two-component endpoint. Cause: the matcher required the contiguous string 'cardiovascular death', and the registry writes 'Cardiovascular (CV) Death' -- an interposed parenthetical abbreviation, which is ubiquitous in registry outcome names.

It produced the RIGHT answer for DELIVER (zero two-component outcomes) for the WRONG reason, and the WRONG answer for EMPEROR. Trusted, it would have implied pool A is k=1. The verdict was checked by READING all 33 registered outcome names across the four trials, not by the matcher.

Class: substring matching over clinical text breaks on parenthetical abbreviations

Published-meta comparison — PENDING_EXTERNAL_RESOLUTION

Denominator: —. Not established, and the obstacle is specific to the three syntheses this review has already identified. 3 published synthes(es) are recorded with their estimates at reconciliation.published_benchmarks, and 3 of them record NO trial_count. The denominator this section requires is how many of THIS review's trials each synthesis included, and it cannot be formed from an estimate alone. A comparison published without it would report the syntheses we happened to find.

Explicitly not done: CITATION-STRING MATCHING. It would produce a comparison-shaped answer immediately and it is not identity: two syntheses citing one trial under different labels read as different trials, and one label on two trials reads as the same trial. That is the substitution class this project audits others for, and it is the reason this section is refused rather than filled.
